Subject: Security questionnaire: PII lineage and KMS key ownership

Hi Alex,

Thanks for moving quickly on the DPA review. Attached is our short spreadsheet to capture how Redwood handles PII lineage, de-identification/tokenization steps, and KMS custody. We have two narrow asks before procurement can sign off:

1) Confirm whether any customer-managed keys are supported for hosted workloads, and if not, explain where key material is stored.
2) A single-page dataflow diagram showing where PII is ingested, transformed, cached (KV/prefix caches), and any persistent storage.

We'd also like a table mapping logical PII classes (PHI/PII/hashed token) to roles that can access the raw values. Please attach any example artifacts (diagram, CSV table).

I've attached: valencia-privacy-questionnaire.xlsx

Best,

Timothy — thanks for the checklist. Quick answers up front: we do support customer-managed keys for Redwood Private and Dedicated; for our hosted API we use a Redwood-managed KMS but with strict separation and HSM-backed storage; I'll include a custody table below and an annotated dataflow.

Attached: redwood-dataflow-diagram-v1.png (PNG, 180KB) — this highlights ingestion points, runtime caches, and short-lived KV caches used for batching.

Two clarifying requests so we can populate your spreadsheet accurately:
- When you say "tokenization", do you mean one-way hashing (irreversible) or reversible token vaults? We treat those differently.
- Do you need per-route access control (e.g., certain endpoints never return original PII even to admins) or is role-level access sufficient?

I'll loop in Neha for the KMS specifics and Laura for contractual mapping to the DPA. Expect an internal confirmation and a consolidated response tomorrow.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Security questionnaire: PII lineage and KMS key ownership — consolidated artifacts

Timothy — thanks for the patience. Consolidated response and artifacts below.

Summary answers (short):
- Hosted API: Redwood-managed HSM-backed keys; keys are scoped per-customer (unique key material per tenant) and we do NOT share key material across customers.
- Rotation cadence: we rotate HSM wrapping keys on a rolling 90-day schedule; underlying HSM key material is rotated per standards with emergency rollover processes.
- BYOK: Supported for Dedicated and Private deployments. We document BYOK steps in the DPA annex; customer-provided keys are used for persistent storage encryption and optional runtime wrapping.
- Operator access: Platform-ops and SRE do NOT have access to decrypted PII. Access matrix below. Security-ops have limited, audited access for incident response with pre-approved JIRA ticket and two-person approval. Customer-support does not have access to raw PII (only redacted or tokenized values).

Attached artifacts: kms-key-ownership-table.csv (CSV, 4KB) — columns: deployment_mode, key_type, custodian, rotation_cadence, notes
redwood-dataflow-diagram-v1.png (annotated)

Operator access (excerpt):
- platform-ops: no
- infra-oncall (SRE): no
- customer-support: no (redacted/tokenized only)
- security-ops: yes (time-limited, audited, on-ticket)
- infra-admin (exec-level): no

We can also provide a signed attestation for key scoping and rotation if Valencia needs it for audit — happy to include as a one-page addendum to the DPA. Let me know if you want that attestation or a redline to the key-custody clause.

Best regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security — Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
